Indoor or outdoor? Start with the application.

Instrument transformers appear in enclosed panels, substations and outdoor metering installations. The location is more than a label: it is part of the application the equipment must be designed to serve.

Where indoor designs are used

Indoor current and voltage transformers are commonly integrated into medium-voltage switchgear. Depending on the design, they can also serve compact secondary substations and other enclosed electrical installations. Their dimensions and arrangement need to work with the host equipment.

Indoor does not automatically mean every enclosed location is suitable. Share the panel layout and installation conditions when discussing a transformer with its manufacturer.

Where outdoor designs are used

Outdoor instrument transformers are used in applications including substations, overhead-line equipment and pole-mounted metering installations. These locations expose equipment to different environmental conditions from those inside a switchgear enclosure.

Outdoor designs use insulation and construction appropriate to their specified service conditions. The actual environmental capability belongs to the individual product specification; it cannot be assumed from a photograph or a product category.

Bring the setting into the conversation

A useful project brief describes both the electrical requirement and the installation. As a practical starting point, gather:

  • The installation type: inside switchgear, within a building or in an outdoor yard.
  • The available mounting space and equipment interface drawings.
  • The site conditions and environmental requirements recorded in the project specification.
  • The metering or protection function and the electrical ratings required.

Compare the right options

ATIPL lists indoor and outdoor current transformers and potential transformers in its product range. Start with the relevant category, then confirm the model and ratings against the project requirements. A clear application brief makes that review more productive.
